verdict.rationale: Sentry's first-party Agent Tracing auto-instruments supported AI libraries and records individual LLM calls with token usage, cost, and response performance. Prompt and response content can be captured via `data_collection` (Python) or `recordInputs`/`recordOutputs` (Node), and traces show durations so latency can be investigated in context. Note that input/output capture is off by default and must be enabled. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of LLM tracing.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: **LLM Calls** shows individual model requests. Use it to compare models, prompts, token usage, cost, and response performance without reviewing an entire conversation or trace.
Prompt and response content is off by default — use the `gen_ai` key of the [`data_collection` option](/platforms/python/configuration/options/#data_collection) to capture it.
You can also set `recordInputs` / `recordOutputs` on a specific AI integration.
Use it to follow execution across model calls, tools, and services or to investigate latency and errors in context.
Below these widgets is a traces table showing trace ID, agents, root duration, errors, LLM calls, tool calls, total tokens, total cost, and timestamp.
Supported AI libraries are instrumented automatically when their packages are installed.
